Macke.et: Borrowed from Yiddish מכּה (make, “plague, wound”), from Hebrew מַכָּה (maká, “blow, wound”), from הִכָּה (hiká, “to hit, to strike”).

Macis.et: From Middle French macis, from Old French macis, from Medieval Latin macis, alteration of Latin macir, from Ancient Greek μάκιρ (mákir).
